summary: Create tagged micro-project namespace with automatic Slack-to-Jira thread bridge for ephemeral teams
description:
Issue summary: Request to build a lightweight, tagged micro-project namespace that automates creation of a Jira project, a seeded Confluence space, and a Slack channel with an opt-in Slack-to-Jira thread bridge.

Background: Several research and infra pods need ephemeral collaboration workspaces for short experiments (1–6 weeks). Manual provisioning creates drift (naming, retention, missing runbooks). This task aims to create a self-service provisioning path that enforces naming/tagging, seeds minimal templates, and wires a thread-bridge so decisions logged in Slack can be optionally recorded in Jira as a linked issue/comment.

Request details:
- New self-service endpoint (internal UI or slash command) that creates: Jira micro-project (templated issue types), Confluence space seeded with runbook and audit checklist, and Slack channel prefixed with team tag.
- Channel naming convention example: team-<tag>-<short-desc>-exp (enforced).
- Thread-bridge behavior: when a user runs `/bridge create` in a thread, a lightweight Jira issue is created and first thread message is added as the issue description; subsequent thread messages are appended as comments. Bridge must be permission-scoped and auditable.
- Default retention and export: channel set to 90-day auto-archive, Confluence seeded with export links and retention metadata.

Business justification: Reduce friction for short-lifecycle experiments while keeping auditability and consistent templates for runbooks and incident seeds. Avoids persistent orphaned channels/projects and accelerates setup time for engineers and research collaborators.

Requirements:
- Service account with minimal scopes for Jira and Confluence provisioning (documented).
- Slack app with OAuth scopes for channel creation and threads API.
- Configurable tagging whitelist (managed by infra admin group).
- Audit trail written to central Confluence or log collection (linkable by ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Owner can provision namespace in < 2 minutes via UI or slash command.
2) Created Jira project uses micro-project template and contains a seeded 'Experiment Runbook' issue.
3) Confluence space contains runbook + exported policy page and a link back to created Jira project.
4) Slack thread-bridge creates Jira issue and appends subsequent messages as comments with author attribution.
5) All artifacts include tagging metadata and are discoverable via the admin index.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - provisioning request rather than a bug
Expected flow: owner invokes provisioning flow and validates artifacts in Jira/Confluence/Slack
Verify thread-bridge: run `/bridge create` in a thread then post follow-ups and confirm comments appear in Jira
investigation_notes: Initial design considered two implementation paths: 1) central provisioning service (preferred) using a single service account and scoped OAuth flow; 2) per-team bot installs (higher isolation, more complexity). We validated that Jira project creation via API requires project-admin role on the service account; Confluence space creation can be accomplished with space-create scope. Slack thread bridging will use conversation.history and chat.postMessage scopes plus a webhook for reliability. Key risk: service account must be documented and rotated; RBAC must prevent cross-tenant tagging abuse. We sketched a PoC that creates a Jira project with key prefix EXP- and seeds a Runbook issue (see related_github_prs).

Izabela Torres (2026-03-13): Recommend we include a 'decommission checklist' step to mark projects for archival and export. Suggest retention 90 days unless owner requests extension.

Evan Zhou (2026-03-14): Implemented initial automation in staging; created smoke test script and documented steps in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/OPS/Ephemeral+Namespace+Provisioner
next_steps: 1) Security to review and approve service account scopes (assigned to Security team). 2) Provisioner team to add configurable tag whitelist and owner claim flow. 3) Build end-to-end smoke tests and run in staging. 4) Schedule 1-week pilot with two pods; collect feedback and adjust retention defaults.
resolution: Design approved by infra on 2026-03-14. Automation implemented in staging; pending security scope sign-off and pilot rollout. No production rollout until audit logging confirmed.
